name: Every Little Thing She Does Is Magic

info.album: The Very Best Of Sting And The Police

podcast.body: The lead single from "Ghost in the Machine," this deeply romantic song became The Police's first "true pop smash," rising to number three on the Hot 100 by the fall of 1981, marking their highest charting hit to date. Sting wrote an early version in 1977 while secretly falling in love with his future wife, Trudy Styler, while still married to his first wife, Francis Tomlty, capturing the feeling of helpless infatuation. Four years later, in collaboration with Copeland, Summers, and producer Hugh Padgham, it gained a lush, uptempo sound, blending Caribbean and new wave elements. Its video, shot in Montserrat, received extensive MTV play and immediate radio rotation. "Every little thing she does is magic. It was a deeply romantic song, but it was not a new song. Sting wrote an early version in 1977 when he was covertly falling in love with his future wife Trudy Styler while married to his first wife, Francis Tomlty."

podcast.body: This single was the trio's biggest hit to date, reaching number three on the Hot 100 in the fall of 1981. The fact that the band had shot "glamorous videos" for all their singles, including this one, certainly contributed to its success, although they were "due for a big hit anyway." "In the fall of 81, the police scored their biggest hit to date with every little thing she does is magic, a number three hit."
